chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said, 'We are in Makkah, or in Al-Madina, or Al-Heera, or the places where merit is hoped for. So, sometimes a man goes out to perform ablution, and another comes and takes his place.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who is first to a place is more rightful to it for his day and his night.'

key_terms.يَوْمَهُ وَ لَيْلَتَهُ: for his day and his night (duration of stay)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on taking someone's place while they are performing ablution in a mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the fiqh of priority (*sabaq*) in public worship spaces, emphasizing that the first person to occupy a spot for ablution holds exclusive rights to it until they finish, preventing displacement. It reflects the practical legal principles of the Shia tradition regarding communal rights and order in holy cities like Mecca, Medina, and Kufa (Al-Hira). The ruling underscores the importance of respecting others' space during ritual acts, fostering a harmonious environment for devotion.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said, ‘We happen to be in Makkah, or in Al-Medina, or Al-Heera, or the places wherein the merit is hoped for. So, sometimes the man goes out to perform ablution and another one comes and takes his place’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who was first to the place, so he is more rightful with it for his day, and his night’.
en.sarwar: 33. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from certain individuals of his people who have said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘We may happen to be in Makkah or al-Madinah or al-Hirah, or in such places where there is hope that there is a degree of excellence for being there. If one goes out for Wudu’, can, in such case, another person come and occupy his place?’
He (the Imam) said, ‘If one finds a place he is more deserving of it for a day and night than others.’”
